subsections.title: Overview
subsections.summary: What it is and why it matters.

blocks.html: Storage privacy is about the devices your data physically lives on: laptops, phones, USB drives and backup disks. If one is lost, stolen or seized, encryption is what keeps the data unreadable. Good habits — encrypting drives, keeping real backups, and wiping old devices properly — protect you against both accidents and attackers.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.summary: The words you will run into.

items.title: Full-disk encryption
items.html: Encrypts a whole drive so nothing on it is readable without the key.

items.title: 3-2-1 backup
items.html: Three copies of your data, on two kinds of media, with one kept somewhere else.

items.title: Secure erase
items.html: Wiping a drive so deleted files can’t be recovered before you sell or recycle it.

items.title: NAS
items.html: Network-attached storage: a small home server that holds files and backups.

items.label: Cryptomator
items.desc: encrypt files and folders before storing them anywhere.
